step_1_scope_the_lever.claim: Only one mechanic in this build can move a PRE-mitigation (raw) damage number.
work: Black Cleaver / Carve (S1) is armor REDUCTION. Per S6 the engine's damage pipeline is post = raw * 100/(100+R): armor only enters through R. Changing Carve stacks (including the Cesaro-mean correction the doc recommends, S7) moves post-mitigation damage and can never move a raw_damage leaf.

Bloodsong / Spellblade (S2) contributes two things: a separate on-hit instance of 100% base AD, and 'Expose Weakness' = +8% (melee) / +5% (ranged) increased damage taken from all sources (S3). An 'increased damage taken' amp is the only multiplier in this build that scales a raw damage instance.
Bloodsong grants no AD (S4), so it cannot change any AD-scaled raw base either; Black Cleaver's 40 AD (S5) is unchanged by any wiki-side reading.
step_1_scope_the_lever.conclusion: Any legitimate change to this leaf must be a change in the Expose Weakness amp factor applied to event 23.

work: Values are golden-rounded to 1 dp, so old in [50.65, 50.75) and new in [45.85, 45.95).
Observed ratio old/new therefore lies in [1.10229, 1.10687] (point estimate 50.7/45.9 = 1.10457).
Multipliers constructible from S2/S3: 1.05, 1.08, and their (buggy) compositions 1.05^2 = 1.1025, 1.08^2 = 1.1664, 1.05*1.08 = 1.134, additive doubles 1.10 / 1.13 / 1.16.
In-band ratios: 1.16/1.05 = 1.10476 (in band, comfortable overlap: base B in [43.67, 43.75]) and 1.05^2/1.00 = 1.1025 (in band only on a 0.01-wide knife edge, B in [45.94, 45.95)).
step_2_admissible_multiplier_family.conclusion: Every in-band reading has the OLD number carrying an over-applied Expose Weakness (either +16% = the melee 8% counted twice additively, or the ranged 5% counted twice multiplicatively), and the NEW number carrying either the single correct ranged 5% (B*1.05 = 45.9, B = 43.71) or no amp at all.

work: Every wiki-consistent correction available here is a REDUCTION of the raw number: 8% -> 5% (wrong side of {{rd|melee|ranged}}), double-count -> single count, or ally-coupled amp applied where it should not be.
There is no wiki-sourced reading in which the correct value EXCEEDS a single-amp application: max legitimate factor is 1.08 (melee) applied once.
50.7 = 45.9 * 1.10457 exceeds 1.08, so 50.7 cannot be a single, correctly-sided Expose Weakness application over any base that also produces 45.9.
step_3_direction_check.conclusion: 50.7 is excluded as the correct value under the cached wiki text; old_value_correct is ruled out.

step_4_best_fit.preferred_reading: raw = B * (1 + 0.05) with B ~= 43.71 (single, ranged-sided Expose Weakness on a ranged Bloodsong holder). The old value corresponds to B * 1.16, i.e. the melee 8% value applied twice additively (8% + 8%).

numbers.agreement: 0.016% - within the 1 dp golden rounding of both leaves

step_4_best_fit.alternate_reading: raw = B (no amp) with B ~= 45.94, old = B * 1.05^2 = 50.65 (ranged 5% double-applied). Numerically admissible but only on a 0.01-wide window; under this reading the new value would be missing a legitimate amp.

sanity_checks_run: Bloodsong Spellblade base component (S2, 100% base AD) checked against every champion at every level 1-20 using the growth law base + growth*(L-1)*(0.7025+0.0175*(L-1)): no champion produces 45.9 or 50.7 as base AD at any plausible fight level (only Orianna L2 = 45.87 and Kennen L2 = 50.70 / Janna L3 = 50.69 land there), so neither leaf is a bare Spellblade proc.

Under the integer stat-rounding convention (S8) both leaves are consistent with 0.30 * AD for integer AD (153 -> 45.9 and 169 -> 50.7), i.e. a 16-AD stat swing; no item in this build (S4, S5) supplies a 16 AD delta, so an AD-stat explanation is not supported by the cached data.
Black Cleaver Cesaro-mean correction (S7) was checked and rejected as the cause: it moves R, hence post-mitigation damage only (S6), never raw.

residual_uncertainty: The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' lives outside the permitted evidence tree (scripts/tests), so the identity of combat event 23 - which champion, which damage instance - could not be pinned from data/ alone. The verdict rests on the multiplier-family argument (step 2/3), which is identity-independent, not on reproducing the base damage B from first principles.

If the fix instead changed the base damage B (e.g. an event-ordering shift that makes events[23] a different instance), the multiplier analysis does not apply; in that case this receipt confirms only the direction, not the magnitude.

The knife-edge alternate reading (1.05^2 -> 1.00) would make the new value un-amped and therefore also wrong; it is disfavoured because it requires the pre-rounding old value to sit inside a 0.01-wide window, whereas the preferred reading has a wide, self-consistent overlap.
